# Narrative Architecture

This file is the index. The cards themselves live in `resources/`, one
file per family. Use the tables below to decide which file to open, then
read that file. Do not load every resource unless the change spans several
families.

Rules that hold across every card:

- Write the beats before choosing words; a structure that is not visible in
  the order of the material is not the structure.
- One structure per piece. A second one competes with the first for the same
  attention.
- The audience's change is the spine: say what they believed before, and what
  they should believe after.

## Arc & Plot (12 cards)

Read `resources/arc-plot.md` for the checks, fixes and sources.

| ID | Card | Apply when |
|---|---|---|
| ARC-01 | Freytag’s Pyramid | Explaining a product lifecycle, a multi-year transformation, or any change with an unavoidable peak of pressure. |
| ARC-02 | Hero’s Journey (Monomyth) | Onboarding journeys, founder stories, and any change that is really someone leaving a familiar state and returning altered. |
| ARC-03 | Harmon Story Circle | Sprint retrospectives, user journey maps, and short case studies where the whole arc has to fit on one slide. |
| ARC-04 | Three-Act Structure | Pitch decks, keynotes, and proposals long enough that the audience needs to know where they are in the argument. |
| ARC-05 | Kishōtenketsu | Product reveals, design retrospectives, and audiences who resist being told there is a problem to defeat. |
| ARC-06 | In Medias Res | Incident briefings and executive updates, where the audience's first question is how bad it is, not how it began. |
| ARC-07 | Man in a Hole | Outage write-ups, security incidents, and turnaround plans where the audience already knows something went wrong. |
| ARC-08 | Rags to Riches | Account expansion case studies, bootstrap histories, and adoption stories where the starting point is the credibility. |
| ARC-09 | Icarus Narrative | Technical-debt reviews, growth retrospectives, and any warning where the audience is proud of the thing being criticised. |
| ARC-10 | Cinderella Arc | Seed-to-scale stories, pilot programmes, and validation narratives where the first success did not hold. |
| ARC-11 | Oedipus Arc | Post-mortems of strategic miscalculations, where the audience needs to see that the cause predates the failure. |
| ARC-12 | The Fichtean Curve | High-volatility scaling narratives, change-management briefings, and talks where attention must be earned every minute. |

## Persuasion & Pitch (12 cards)

Read `resources/persuasion-pitch.md` for the checks, fixes and sources.

| ID | Card | Apply when |
|---|---|---|
| PRS-01 | Aristotle’s Rhetorical Triangle | Board briefings and stakeholder memos, where being right is not yet being persuasive. |
| PRS-02 | Monroe’s Motivated Sequence | Sales pitches and budget approvals, where the audience must leave with a specific next step. |
| PRS-03 | Duarte’s Sparkline | Visionary keynotes and strategic realignments, where the case is a change of direction rather than a fix. |
| PRS-04 | The Pitch Canvas | Seed and Series A presentations, where the audience is deciding whether the opportunity is real. |
| PRS-05 | Problem-Agitation-Solution (PAS) | Executive summaries and sales cadences where the reader is already busy and already sceptical. |
| PRS-06 | Before-After-Bridge (BAB) | Cold outreach, case studies and transformation proposals, where the reader must want the after before hearing the how. |
| PRS-07 | The Story Spine | Sixty-second pitches and investor teasers, where the whole story must fit in one breath. |
| PRS-08 | The 10/20/30 Venture Pattern | Formal venture partner meetings, where attention is short and the room has read a hundred decks that month. |
| PRS-09 | The Insight-Led Challenge | Complex B2B sales conversations, where the buyer believes their current approach is already reasonable. |
| PRS-10 | Strategic Narrative Architecture | Category creation and enterprise positioning, where the question is not which vendor but which future. |
| PRS-11 | Socratic Elenchus | Architecture disputes among technical stakeholders who will accept a conclusion they reached and reject one they were handed. |
| PRS-12 | The Golden Circle | Employer branding and brand positioning, where comparable products compete and the difference is purpose. |

## Corporate & Technical (12 cards)

Read `resources/corporate-technical.md` for the checks, fixes and sources.

| ID | Card | Apply when |
|---|---|---|
| COR-01 | Blameless Post-Mortem Arc | Production incident reviews and operational reporting, where the next incident must be cheaper than this one. |
| COR-02 | Product Vision Narrative | New product vetting and zero-to-one allocation, where the decision is whether the outcome is worth funding. |
| COR-03 | Customer Success Trajectory | Customer advocacy decks and retention reviews, where the claim is that the customer now works differently. |
| COR-04 | Architectural Decision Record (ADR) | Architecture council submissions and technical governance, where a later engineer will ask why this way. |
| COR-05 | Enterprise Crucible Myth | Culture handbooks and leadership transitions, where stated values need a decision behind them. |
| COR-06 | Technical Debt Reckoning | Refactoring proposals and engineering re-allocation, where velocity has slowed and no one agrees why. |
| COR-07 | Sunset & Deprecation Eulogy | System retirement briefings and API deprecation notices, where users must migrate rather than stall. |
| COR-08 | M&A Integration Thesis | Mergers, acquisitions and internal reorganisations, where the synergy case must survive contact with two cultures. |
| COR-09 | Digital Transformation Arc | Enterprise transformation updates and board reporting, where the current business is both the sponsor and the obstacle. |
| COR-10 | Regulatory Compliance Crucible | Audit committee defence and compliance budget requests, where the exposure is real and the evidence is thin. |
| COR-11 | The Innovation Horizon Brief | Annual R&D allocation and innovation reviews, where the current business always wins the budget argument. |
| COR-12 | Turnaround Restructuring Thesis | Turnaround memos and distressed unit reviews, where the audience is deciding how much time exists. |

## Rhetorical Micro-tactic (12 cards)

Read `resources/rhetorical-micro-tactic.md` for the checks, fixes and sources.

| ID | Card | Apply when |
|---|---|---|
| MIC-01 | The In Medias Res Hook | Slide one and the executive summary, where the reader may stop after the first line. |
| MIC-02 | Polarity Shift (Contrast & Tension) | Slides making urgency felt, where a flat list of risks has stopped registering. |
| MIC-03 | Sensory Detail Anchoring | Explaining latency, scale or KPI movement to an audience that does not work with the number. |
| MIC-04 | Metaphorical Bridge | Explaining distributed consensus, machine learning or queueing to a mixed audience. |
| MIC-05 | Anagnorisis (The Aha-Moment) | Research reveals and strategic unveilings, where the conclusion must feel discovered rather than asserted. |
| MIC-06 | The Call to Adventure | Closing slides and all-hands conclusions, where agreement exists but nothing has been asked for. |
| MIC-07 | Identifiable Victim Effect | Funding cases for accessibility, safety or user experience, where the aggregate number has stopped persuading. |
| MIC-08 | Tricolon (Rule of Three) | Speechwriting, mission statements and value definitions, where a line must be repeated out loud. |
| MIC-09 | Chekhov’s Gun | Strategy narratives and technical differentiators foreshadowed before they matter. |
| MIC-10 | Zeigarnik Tension Loop | Multi-part updates and town halls, where the audience's attention must survive several sections. |
| MIC-11 | Reductio Ad Absurdum | Discrediting inaction or the defence of a legacy system, where the audience believes the status quo is stable. |
| MIC-12 | The Counterfactual Pivot | Security, risk and compliance ROI cases, where prevention has no visible outcome to point at. |

Every card cites a primary source or names the tradition it comes from; the citation travels with the card.
